```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
  fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5
)
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)
library(pracma)
library(isotone)
```

# 1. Goal and set-up

We estimate the expected cost-effectiveness of pre-positioned PPE in terms of dollars per HCW life saved. To do so, we combine:

1) A baseline LMIC PPE CE estimate during COVID-19 ([source](https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0240503)),  
   \[
   \mathrm{CE}_{\text{COVID}} \approx \$4{,}309 \text{ per HCW life}.
   \]

2) A distribution of mortailty risk from respiratory pandemics (deaths per 10k population, \(D\)) from [Madhav et al.](https://www.cgdev.org/publication/estimated-future-mortality-pathogens-epidemic-and-pandemic-potential), summarized by the **exceedance function**  
   \[
   E(d) = \Pr(D \ge d).
   \]

We assume that PPE cost-effectiveness decreases with pandemic severity \(D\). To be conservative, we let CE fall linearly with \(D\) below COVID severity and only with the square-root above it:

\[
\mathrm{CE}(D) =
\begin{cases}
\mathrm{CE}_{\text{COVID}} \;\dfrac{D_{\text{COVID}}}{D}, & D \le D_{\text{COVID}} \\[8pt]
\mathrm{CE}_{\text{COVID}} \;\sqrt{\dfrac{D_{\text{COVID}}}{D}}, & D > D_{\text{COVID}}.
\end{cases}
\]

```{r inputs}
CE_COVID <- 1 / 4309
severity_COVID  <- 14.86e6 / (7.86e9 / 1e4) # Excess deaths between 2020-2021 (WHO) divided by 2020 global population
CE_COVID; severity_COVID
```

```{r read-data}
mraw <- read_csv("./data/raw/madhav_et_al_figure_4_digitized.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
mx <- mraw[-1, c(1, 2)]
colnames(mx) <- c("deaths_per_10k", "annual_risk_percent")

mx <- mx %>%
  mutate(
    deaths_per_10k = as.numeric(deaths_per_10k),
    annual_risk    = as.numeric(annual_risk_percent) / 100
  ) %>%
  arrange(deaths_per_10k)
```

# 2. Fit exceedance function

```{r fit-exceedance}
severity_grid <- seq(min(mx$deaths_per_10k), max(mx$deaths_per_10k), length.out = 800)
spline_fit <- splinefun(x = mx$deaths_per_10k, y = mx$annual_risk)
approx_fit <- approxfun(mx$deaths_per_10k, mx$annual_risk, rule = 2)

spline_pred <- spline_fit(severity_grid)
approx_pred <- approx_fit(severity_grid)

ggplot() +
  geom_point(data = mx, aes(deaths_per_10k, annual_risk), size = 1.5) +
  geom_line(aes(severity_grid, spline_pred, color = "Spline"), linewidth = 1) +
  geom_line(aes(severity_grid, approx_pred, color = "Approx"), linewidth = 1, linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Spline" = "blue", "Approx" = "red")) +
  labs(
    x = "Deaths per 10k",
    y = "% Annual risk",
    title = "Exceedance curve",
    color = "Fit"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

Both interpolation techniques fit the data very precisely. We will move forward with approximate for simplicity.

# 3. CE scaling function

```{r ce-scaling}
CE_at_severity <- function(severity) {
  ifelse(
    severity <= severity_COVID,
    CE_COVID * (severity / severity_COVID),
    CE_COVID * sqrt(severity / severity_COVID)
  )
}

ggplot(data.frame(severity = severity_grid)) +
  geom_line(aes(severity, CE_at_severity(severity))) +
  labs(x = "Deaths per 10k", y = "Cost-effectiveness [$ per HCW life]",
       title = "Piecewise CE scaling (linear below, sqrt above)") +
  theme_minimal()
```

# 4. Approach A — PDF route

```{r pdf-route}
exceedance_deriv <- gradient(approx_pred, severity_grid)
fseverity_grid <- -exceedance_deriv
p_event <- trapz(severity_grid, fseverity_grid) # Should be around 0.058

CE_grid <- CE_at_severity(severity_grid)
CE_uncond  <- trapz(severity_grid, CE_grid * fseverity_grid)
```

# Aggregate over 20 year time ----------

```{r}
years <- 20 # Number of years of protection
discount_rate <- 0.04

beta <- 1 / (1 + discount_rate)
discount_weights <- beta^(0:(years - 1))

PV_ce <- sum(discount_weights) * CE_uncond
1 / PV_ce
```
